text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Aqaba today and calls for an easing of Israel's closure of the Palestinian territories.
- The Interior Ministry is working so hard to register all voters for the November elections, it even worked through Monday's public holiday.
- King Hussein says door of dialogue is open and he hopes Jordan's Islamists will share in building the country.
- Moslem Brotherhood, which called for a boycott of parliamentary elections, says it will take part in dialogue if the government is serious about getting out of the current political crisis.
- Parliamentary speaker Saed Hayel Srour says he succeeded in reopening dialogue with Islamists; talks to start "in the near future".
- Cabinet approves regulations under the 1997 Companies Law granting Industry Ministry official supervision of registration of companies.
- Final signing in Amman today of agreement for Jordan Phosphate Mines Company's $100 million eurobond offer.
- Hamas spokesman in Amman says military wing responsible for Jerusalem double suicide bombing.
